brief.title: Generative AI Competitive Landscape: User Sentiment & Complaint Analysis Across Top 5 AI Apps (Q1 2026)
brief.one_liner: A comprehensive competitive analysis of 50,000 user reviews across ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, Perplexity, and Claude, examining sentiment patterns, thematic complaints, and user satisfaction drivers.
brief.goal: Enable the product strategy team to understand how each generative AI application is perceived by mobile users, identify key pain points (pricing, bugs, accuracy) per competitor, detect sentiment-rating mismatches that signal sarcasm or complex user emotions, and derive actionable insights for product positioning and improvement priorities.

required_sections.title: Executive Overview
required_sections.objective: Summarize the overall dataset scope, key findings across all five AI apps, and the top 3 strategic takeaways for the product team.

required_sections.title: Cross-App Sentiment Comparison
required_sections.objective: Compare average star ratings, mean VADER sentiment polarity, and rating distributions across all five applications. Identify which app leads in user satisfaction and which trails.

required_sections.title: Thematic Complaint Analysis by Application
required_sections.objective: Break down the Review_Theme distribution (Pricing, Bugs, Accuracy, General) per app. Determine which competitor suffers most from accuracy/hallucination complaints versus pricing/paywall complaints versus bug/performance issues.

required_sections.title: Sentiment-Rating Divergence & Sarcasm Detection
required_sections.objective: Identify reviews where star ratings and VADER sentiment polarity diverge significantly (e.g., 5-star reviews with negative polarity, or 1-star reviews with positive polarity). Quantify the prevalence of such mismatches per app and discuss implications for review trustworthiness.

required_sections.title: Review Depth & Emotional Intensity
required_sections.objective: Analyze the relationship between Word_Count/Review_Length_Chars and sentiment polarity or star rating. Determine whether dissatisfied users write longer reviews and whether review engagement (Thumbs_Up_Count) correlates with review length or sentiment.

required_sections.title: Strategic Recommendations
required_sections.objective: Synthesize findings into 4-6 prioritized, actionable recommendations for product strategy, addressing competitive positioning, feature improvement areas, and user retention risks.

kpis.name: Average Star Rating by App
kpis.description: Mean star rating (1-5) for each of the five AI applications, indicating overall user satisfaction.

kpis.name: Mean Sentiment Polarity by App
kpis.description: Average VADER compound sentiment score (-1.0 to +1.0) per application, providing a text-derived satisfaction measure independent of star ratings.

kpis.name: Complaint Theme Rate
kpis.description: Percentage of reviews flagged as Pricing, Bugs, or Accuracy themes (vs. General) per app, indicating the prevalence of specific pain points.

kpis.name: Sentiment-Rating Mismatch Rate
kpis.description: Proportion of reviews where star rating and sentiment polarity are contradictory (e.g., high stars but negative polarity or vice versa), signaling sarcasm or complex user sentiment.

kpis.name: Average Review Engagement (Thumbs Up)
kpis.description: Mean Thumbs_Up_Count per app and per theme, indicating which types of feedback resonate most with other users.
